Petition under Section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation Award
1.

The petitioners have filed the present claim petition U/s 166/140 M.V Act, seeking compensation
to the tune of Rs. 3,16,00,000/- from the date of accident till its realization for the fatal injury
sustained by Sh. Tejvir Macp No. 84/21; Fir No. 446/20 Dod: 03.12.2025 Singh, aged about 40
years in Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 16.11.2020 at about 9:00 Pm at Eastern
Peripheral Expressway, Rataul Bypass, Khekda, District Baghpat, Up, involving Car bearing
registration no. As01-Br-4171 (offending vehicle) which was being driven by its driver/respondent
no.1 in a rash and negligent manner.

2. The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim are that on 16.11.2020, deceased
Sh. Tejvir Singh was standing at Eastern Peripheral Expressway, Rataul Bypass, Khekda, District
Baghpat, Up, due to mechanical defect in his car no. Dl8Cy-1423 and the parking lights of his car
were On and he was waiting for help.
At about 9:00 pm, one Xuv Car bearing registration no.

As01-Br-4171 which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent
manner

, came and hit against the aforesaid car of deceased with a great force, as a result of which,
deceased sustained serious injuries.
His postmortem was conducted at Hospital.

A case U/s
279/304A/427 Ipc was registered at Ps. Khekda vide Fir No. 446/2020 with regard to the accident
in question.

The petitioners have claimed that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent
driving of aforementioned offending vehicle which was allegedly being driven by respondent
no.2/driver.

The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 1 and was insured with
respondent no. 3 at the time of accident in question.

They also failed to appear and were proceeded exparte

4.

In its Written Statement, the respondent no. 3 i.e. insurance company has claimed that deceased
himself was negligent as he was standing on the road and there was no involvement of alleged
offending vehicle and the same has been falsely implicated in the present case.

It has been admitted
that offending vehicle was insured with it at the time of accident.

On merits, it has denied the
averments made in the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.

5. From the pleadings of the parties and the documents, following issues were framed vide order
dated 08.11.2023:-
1) Whether deceased Tejvir Singh has died in road side accident occurred on
16.11.2020 at 9:00 Pm at Eastern Peripheral Expressway, Rataul Bypass, Khekda,
District Baghpat, Up, within the jurisdiction of Ps. Khekda, District Baghpat, Up, due
to rashness and negligence on the part of Sh. Narender Pal Singh/R2 who was driving
vehicle bearing registration no. As-01-Br-4171, owned by Sh. Nabab Singh/R1 and
insured with New India Assurance Co. Ltd./R3?OPP.
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation if so, to what extent and
from which of the respondents?
Opp.

3) Relief.
6.
To substantiate their claim, the petitioners have examined two witnesses
i.e. Sh. Ishwar Singh (Father of deceased) as PW-1 and Sh. Satish Kumar (official from Income Tax Department) as PW-2 and their evidence was closed vide order dated 02.04.2025.
On the other hand, no evidence was adduced by any of the respondents and RE in the matter was closed vide order dated 09.07.2025.
7. This Tribunal has carefully perused claim petition, evidence led by petitioners has been duly appreciated.
All documents and material relied upon perused and considered.
Arguments addressed by counsels for the petitioners and insurance company considered.
Legal position, both statutory and binding applicable precedents, has been appreciated.

The issue wise determination is as under:-

sentences.text: 10. Counsel for petitioners heavily relied upon the criminal case record (Ex. PW1/1 to Ex. PW1/5) in order to bring home his point that the accident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing registration no. AS01-BR-4171.

He further argued that FIR No. 446/2020 was registered at PS. Khekra and respondent no. 2 was also chargesheeted by police for offences punishable U/s 279/304A/427 IPC, which clearly establish that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of aforesaid vehicle by respondent no. 2.
11.

On the other hand, counsel for insurance company vehemently argued that PW1 Sh. Ishwar Singh is undisputedly not an eye witness of the accident in question and no eye witness has been examined by petitioners during the course of inquiry.

He, therefore, contended that the petitioners have failed to prove that the accident in question was caused due to rash and negligent driving of aforesaid vehicle by respondent no. 2.
MACP No. 84/21; FIR No. 446/20 DOD: 03.12.2025 12.
Now, turning back to the facts of the present case.

No doubt, the petitioners have not examined any eye witness to prove the negligence on the part of driver of the alleged vehicle described above but nevertheless, there is ample material brought on record during the course of inquiry, which is sufficient to establish that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing registration no. AS01-BR-4171 by its driver.

It is relevant to note here that GD No. 002 was recorded at PS. Khekra on 17.11.2020 at about 12:59 AM on the statement of one Sh. Vikas (brother of deceased) regarding accident in question being caused by one unknown vehicle.

Further, GD No.
003 was recorded at PS. Khekra on 17.11.2020 at about 1:11 AM on the statement of Sh. Nabab Singh (registered owner of offending vehicle) who stated that his vehicle had hit with divider in order to save other vehicle.
A bare perusal of both the aforesaid GDs show that the same were recorded within a short span of 12 minutes and were about the accident which had occurred at the same place on the same date.

Though, in the GD No. 002 the vehicle number which hit the vehicle of deceased was not disclosed, however, contents of GD No. 003 shows that the alleged offending vehicle bearing no. AS01-BR-4171 was being driven by its driver at a very high speed and in negligent manner.
13. Moreover, it is an undisputed fact that FIR No. 446/2020 u/s 279/304A/427 IPC was registered at PS. Khekra with regard to accident in question.
Copy of said FIR (Ex. PW1/1), would show that same was MACP No. 84/21; FIR No. 446/20 DOD: 03.12.2025 registered on 17.11.2020(accident being caused on 16.11.2020 at 9:00 PM.
Thus, FIR is shown to have been registered promptly and without any delay.
After conclusion of investigation, the chargesheet was also filed against respondent no. 2.
Hence, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 2 and/or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioners herein.

On the other hand,
respondents have not examined any witness in order to rebut the testimony of PW1 in this regard during the course of inquiry.
Hence, there is no reason to disbelieve his uncontroverted testimony on the point of accident in question being caused by respondent no. 2 due to his rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.

The injuries as noted in the relevant column with regard to external injuries, as mentioned therein, are consistent with the injuries which are sustained in motor vehicular accident.
Again, there is no challenge to the aforesaid document from the side of respondents.

16. Further, it is well settled legal position as laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court as well as by various High Courts in plethora of judgments delivered from time to time that in claim petitions preferred U/s 160/144 M.V Act, the claimants have to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of alleged offending vehicles by its drivers.
Same is the essence of legal position discussed by Hon'ble Apex Court in celebrated case of Meena Variyal mentioned supra.

At the same time, it is no more res-integra that claim petition filed under relevant provisions of M.V Act, is the outcome of social welfare legislation and the proceedings are summary in nature and do not require strict compliance of rules of evidence and pleadings.
It needs no emphasis that in case replies filed by respondents, are evasive then it is deemed that they have admitted the averments made by the claimants.

The purpose of granting compensation is to ameliorate the sufferings of the victims of Motor Vehicle Accidents and the niceties, hyper technicalities, procedural wrangles and tangles and mystic maybes have no role to play and MACP No. 84/21; FIR No. 446/20 DOD: 03.12.2025 same should not be any ground to dismiss the claim petitions and to defeat the rights of the claimants.

While saying so, I am fortified by the decisions rendered by Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases titled as " N.KV. Bros (P) Ltd Vs. M.
Karumai Ammal", 1980 ACJ 435 (SC); " Sohan Lal Passi Vs. P. Sesh Reddy", 1996 ACJ 1044 (SC)
and " Dulcina Fernandes Vs. Joaquim Xavier Cruz", 2013 ACJ 2712 (SC).

18. In the above cited decision, the facts were almost similar and the claimants had not examined any eyewitness.

Hon'ble Apex Court held that in view of filing of criminal case record including charge-sheet showing that MACP No. 84/21; FIR No. 446/20 DOD: 03.12.2025 driver of alleged offending vehicle had been charge-sheeted for causing the accident due to rash and negligent driving of said vehicle and the driver himself did not enter into witness box, claimants were able to prove the issue of accident being caused due to rash and negligent driving of said vehicle by said driver on the basis of pre-ponderance of the probabilities.

19. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioners have been able to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that deceased Tejvir Singh had sustained fatal injuries in the road accident which took place on 16.11.2020 at about 9:00 PM at Eastern Peripheral Expressway, Rataul Bypass, Khekda, District Baghpat, UP, due to rash and negligent driving on the part of respondent no. 2/driver of the offending vehicle.

Thus,
this issue is decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.

20. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.

The guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" in fatal case has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case titled as Smt. Anjali & Ors.,
Vs. Lokendra Rathod & Ors, in Civil Appeal No. 9014 of 202, decided on 06.12.2022

sentences.text: that: -

MACP No. 84/21; FIR No. 446/20 DOD: 03.12.2025 "The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (for short, "MV Act") gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair'
compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the MV Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the applicant/s.

In Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.3, this Court has laid down as under:
"16."Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.

17. Assessment of compensation though involving certain hypothetical considerations, should nevertheless be objective.
Justice and justness emanate from equality in treatment, consistency and thoroughness in adjudication, and fairness and uniformity in the decision making process and the decisions.
While it may not be possible to have mathematical precision or identical awards, in assessing compensation, same or similar facts should lead to awards in the same range.

When the factors/inputs are the same, and the formula/legal principles are the same, consistency and uniformity, and not divergence and freakiness, should be the result of adjudication to arrive at just compensation..."
22.
The Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance.

25. In order to prove the earnings of the deceased, the petitioners have examined PW2 Sh. Satish Kumar, from the office of Income Tax Department.
PW2 produced the ITR of deceased Tejvir Singh for the Assessment Years 2017-18, 2018-19 & 2020-21 and exhibited the same as Ex. PW2/B(colly).
During his cross-examination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that the document brought by him on that day Ex. PW2/B have been downloaded from the portal of income tax.
He further deposed that the computer from which it has been downloaded was under his control and password was known to him.
He further deposed that he had not brought any certificate under BNS qua digital evidence.
He denied the suggestion that the record brought by him was not genuine or that the same was false and fabricated.
He admitted that the said record was not assessed physically by the department.
He volunteered that 0.25% of cases were selected by the software for physical assessment/checking the ITR.
He admitted that the calculation sheet was not brought by him on that day.
He volunteered that the same was not required to be kept in the ITR where the turnover was less than 2 crores.
He further deposed that there was no record available with their department after 2019-20.

After referring to the testimonies of PW1 & PW2 and the documents filed by the said witnesses,
Ld. counsel for petitioners vehemently argued that annual income of deceased should be taken as Rs. 5,25,000/-.

For said purpose, he relied upon ITRs for the Years 2017-18, 2018-19, 2019-20 &
2020-21 (Ex. PW2/B colly) filed on record.
He, therefore, urged that appropriate amount of compensation may be awarded on the basis of said ITRs.

On the other hand, Ld. counsel for insurance company vehemently argued that the petitioner has failed to lead any cogent evidence to prove his actual income at the time of accident and thus, his income may be taken as per Minimum Wages Act applicable during the relevant period.

27. The aforesaid argument raised on behalf of insurance company, is not tenable in the eyes of law for the simple reason that the deceased was an income tax assessee and was filing ITRs since much prior to the date of accident.
A bare perusal of said ITRs reveals that the gross income of deceased during the respective periods of ITRs were almost similar.

sentences.text: PW1 has categorically deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A) that all the petitioners were financially dependent upon the income of deceased.
It is stated that the deceased was survived by three dependents i.e. parents and son of deceased.
It may be noted here that PW1/father of deceased himself deposed in his cross-examination that he had not filed the death certificate of wife of deceased.

During the course of arguments, it was pointed out that the wife of deceased had already expired and in lieu of the same, death verification report of wife of deceased was called from the concerned SHO and upon verification, it was found that wife of deceased had expired in December, 2022.

Even otherwise, it was also argued that wife of the deceased had left the house of deceased long time back before the death of deceased and deceased was survived by only three LRs i.e., his parents and son.

Thus, it is held that the deceased was survived by three dependents at the time of accident who are his parents and son and hence one third is liable to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of deceased.
Thus, the total of loss of dependency would come out to Rs. 60,39,375/- (Rs. 4,83,150/- X 2/3 X 125/100 X 15).

Hence, a sum of Rs.
60,39,375/- is awarded under this head in favour of the petitioners.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
No doubt, the petitioners have not examined any eye witness to prove the negligence on the part of driver of the alleged vehicle described above but nevertheless, there is ample material brought on record during the course of inquiry, which is sufficient to establish that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing registration no. AS01-BR-4171 by its driver.
Hence, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 2 and/or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioners herein.
On the other hand,
respondents have not examined any witness in order to rebut the testimony of PW1 in this regard during the course of inquiry.
Hence, there is no reason to disbelieve his uncontroverted testimony on the point of accident in question being caused by respondent no. 2 due to his rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.

Further, there is no gainsaying that respondent No.1/driver of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no. 2.
There is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case.

The purpose of granting compensation is to ameliorate the sufferings of the victims of Motor Vehicle Accidents and the niceties, hyper technicalities, procedural wrangles and tangles and mystic maybes have no role to play and MACP No. 84/21; FIR No. 446/20 DOD: 03.12.2025 same should not be any ground to dismiss the claim petitions and to defeat the rights of the claimants.
While saying so, I am fortified by the decisions rendered by Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases titled as " N.KV. Bros (P) Ltd Vs. M.
Karumai Ammal", 1980 ACJ 435 (SC); " Sohan Lal Passi Vs. P. Sesh Reddy", 1996 ACJ 1044 (SC)
and " Dulcina Fernandes Vs. Joaquim Xavier Cruz", 2013 ACJ 2712 (SC).
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the MV Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.
Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the applicant/s.
In Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.3, this Court has laid down as under:
"16."Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.
The intent and objective of the Beneficial Legislation is to grant equitable compensation to the vulnerable victims of road accidents and dynamic law has evolved towards grant of just and fair quantum of awards and has brought consistency and uniformity towards the desired goal.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009) 6 SCC 121, which was affirmed by a bench of three Hon'ble Judges in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs. Madan Mohan & Anr.,

The aforesaid Principle of law has also been reiterated by a landmark judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme court in 2017 (13) SCALE 12 : 2017 XI AD (SC) 113 titled National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.
Accordingly, the quantum of appropriate and adequate compensation to the victims of road accident is to be derived after assessment of various relevant parameters, as per law.

It is also relevant to mention here that while deciding claim petition under M.V Act, it is the duty of Claims Tribunal to follow the principles of justice, equity and good conscience and to adopt more realistic, pragmatic and liberal approach.
